To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the virus was found to be present in hepatocytes and in a few macrophages close by the areas of inflammation in 6-week-old rabbits, but in only a few hepatocyte in 12-week-old rabbits, and in 12-week old rabbits the viral antigen was present in hepatocytes, macrophages and a few lymphocytes.

VP60 was detected as early at 12 hpi and in a few hepatocyte from adult rabbits; VP60 was detected in hepatocytes and in some macrophages from young rabbits; and extrahepatic viral antigen was detected at 36 hpi in macrophages and some lymphocytes from spleens of adult rabbits.

VP60 was not detected in tissues from animals under four week, only a few hepatocyte was stained in the 8 week-old animals, a 8 week-old rabbit euthanized at 72 h showed VP60-labeled hepatocyte and macrophage close to areas of inflamation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the immunohistochemical localisations of RHDV VP60 antigen in tissues from experimentaly infected young (3, 4 and 6 weeks) and adult rabbits (8 to 12 weeks).
the early events of the RHDV infection, which are important to understand the pathogenesis of the disease and to develop new control measures.
the study of the pathogenesis of RHDV in young and adult rabbits, and with the evaluation of the time course distribution and tissue tropism of viral VP60 antigen in early stages of the infection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the age of the host is the main factor determining RHDV VP60 antigen distribution in the early stages of the disease.
VP60 is not detectable until 18 hours post infection in adult rabbits, and is not detected at all in young rabbits.
the liver is the only target organ of RHDV, and that RHDV VP60 antigen can be detected in the liver and in the spleen of infected adult rabbits as soon as 12 h post infection (hpi).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the liver is the only organ that is able to support the replication of RHDV in rabbits.

RHDV VP60 protein is detected in a small number of hepatocytes from young animals, but is detected at a high frequency in hepatocytes and in extrahepatic cells from adult animals, suggesting that age may be a factor in the susceptibility of the host to RHDV infection.

the VP60 antigen of the RHDV is a very good target for immunohistochemical analysis, and that the virus can be detected in the hepatocytes of young animals as early as 18 hpi, and in adult animals as early as12 hpi.
The main takeaway from our work is that
VP60 antigen is not present in tissues from young rabbits.
the liver is a primary target for RHDV infection and that the virus is able to infect and replicate in a small proportion of hepatocytes within 12 h of infection.
VP60 antigen is detectable at early times post-infection in adult animals, which is consistent with the high susceptibility of adult rabbits to RHDV.
